tools.name: search
tools.description: Find domain names for an idea. Returns candidate names across every ending, each with the state we can defend: sellable, restricted, not ours to sell, taken, or not checked. Pass the concept, not a domain.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Everything we hold about one domain: whether it is registered, what it costs to claim AND what it renews at, and where each number came from. Pass a domain name as the id, for example "atlas.io".

tools.name: create_draft
tools.description: Stores a draft website in the user's Scopeweb portfolio and returns a persistent draft_id and a live preview_url. tools.name: update_draft
tools.description: Writes a new version of an existing draft. Acts as a patch: files you send are written as a new version, files you omit carry forward unchanged, and earlier versions are kept. tools.name: list_drafts
tools.description: Lists every draft in the user's Scopeweb portfolio with status, preview URL and timestamps. For when the user asks about existing pages or wants to resume earlier work. Read-only. Cannot spend money.

tools.name: get_draft
tools.description: Returns a draft's metadata and file list, or a single file's content when path is given. For reading the current text of a draft, including one made in an earlier conversation. Read-only. Cannot spend money.

tools.name: verify_ownership
tools.description: Proves the user controls a domain with a DNS TXT challenge. action 'start' returns the TXT record to publish; action 'check' looks for it. For when the user says a domain is theirs and the claim matters. A verified domain joins the user's inventory. A failed DNS lookup returns an error, never 'not o

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: Lists the user's domain inventory: every domain with a verification challenge issued or completed, with cached liveness, classification, title and expiry. For portfolio, renewal and 'what do I own' questions. Each entry carries scan_age_ms, so a stale verdict reads as stale. Read-only. Cannot spend

tools.name: suggest_names
tools.description: Generates candidate names across a namespace from a concept (a word or short phrase) and classifies each by what the registry says: unregistered, registered, pending or unprobed. For when the user is choosing or inventing a name and wants options to look at. Pending and unprobed are never registrati

tools.name: recommend_name
tools.description: Runs the whole naming job on the server and returns one recommended domain with its real price and a confirm_url, plus runners-up. tools.name: score_name
tools.description: Grades candidate names on measurable properties of the string: length, syllables, pronounceability (the radio test), presence in a published English word list, edit distance to major brands, hyphens and digits, and TLD perception. For when the user is choosing between names or asks whether one is an

tools.name: scan_namespace
tools.description: Classifies an explicit list of up to 25 domains: registered, resolves, serves, parked, classification and liveness for each. For when the user already has specific names rather than a concept. Read-only. Cannot spend money.

tools.name: check_live
tools.description: Checks up to 10 domains against the registry in real time (RDAP) and reports whether each is registered right now. For confirming availability just before a recommendation or purchase decision, and for any name an earlier answer marked 'unknown', 'pending' or 'unprobed', which are never registration

tools.name: audit_domain
tools.description: Fetches a live domain's observable surface: HTTP status, redirect target, title, meta description, h1 headings and tech hints. For when the user asks what is wrong with a site they own, what is deployed at a domain, or whether it serves anything at all. Read-only. Cannot spend money.

tools.name: set_budget
tools.description: Records a monthly or yearly spending ceiling, in cents, for one of the user's projects by project_id. For when the user states a spending limit. tools.name: get_finance
tools.description: The financial readout for one project: the budget, per-domain renewal costs, total known carry, how many domains have unknown renewal costs, and remaining headroom. For questions about what a project costs to hold or how much budget is left. Domains held at another registrar renew at that registrar'

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Lists the projects this account owns or operates through an entity, with each project_id and how many domains and drafts each holds, plus a count of verified domains not filed in any project. For when the user refers to a project, or wants a budget or finance readout, and its project_id is not known

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Creates a named project owned by this account and returns its project_id. For when the user starts something new and wants a budget or its costs tracked. Cannot spend money.

tools.name: kb_search
tools.description: Semantic search over a small curated corpus: Scopeweb's own documentation and methodology, ICANN policy, and per-registry policy documents. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_drafts, kb_search · Private data: update_draft, get_draft, verify_ownership, set_budget, kb_search · Public sink: update_draft, verify_ownership.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_drafts, kb_search · Private data: update_draft, get_draft, verify_ownership, set_budget, kb_search · Public sink: update_draft, verify_ownership

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
